_comment: Maryland 2026, DHCD/CDA. Scoring is Chapter 4 of the Multifamily Rental Financing Program Guide (this file); the QAP (maryland-qap-2026.pdf) is bundled for context and defers scoring to the Guide. Page numbers are PDF page indices; printed 'Page | n' is PDF page n+5. The Scoring Summary Table (p.59) states 221 points: 74 + 16 + 8 + 55 + 25 + 33 + 10. Hand-summed before loading: 4.1 = 42 + 18 + 14 = 74 (the -10 deduction excluded); 4.2 = 16 (one of three); 4.3 = 8; 4.4 = 5 + 10 + 10 + 8 + 8 + 10 + 4 = 55; 4.5 = 15 + 10 = 25 (the -8 cost deduction excluded); 4.6 = 10 + 6 + 13 + 4 = 33; 4.7 = 10. Total 221, matching. State Bonus Points (4.8) sit 'outside of the 221 point scale' and go on their own track. No tiebreakers are stated in either document. Minimum scores (pp.57-58): 92 for MBP/RHW-only projects, with category minimums; 145 for the Infill and Redevelopment Pool. Contradictions recorded in notes: 4.1.4's name (MBE/DBEs vs Local Small Businesses), 4.6.1's name, the 4.5.2 worked example, the misplaced 4.4.3 example, the State Bonus maximum (10 vs 15), and the Tennessee data source in 4.2.2. Thresholds are in MD_thresholds.json.

track_totals.note: Scoring Summary Table total. Excludes the -10 and -8 deductions and the State Bonus.
Discretionary, outside the 221-point scale. 10, or 15 for intergenerational, elderly or supportive housing.

criteria.note: Each of four team members is rated on one of four rows (the last row, 'limited or no experience', scores 0 for all). 18 + 9 + 6 + 9 = 42. MBP/RHW-only projects need at least 30 here (32 with FHA Risk Sharing), p.57.

criteria.note: Developer up to 6, property manager up to 4, for listed performance failures in the past five years. Scored as 'Negative 10 points' in the Scoring Summary Table (p.59), outside the 221.

criteria.quote: Up to eighteen (18) points may be awarded based on the financial capacity of the Developer,

tiers.tier_label: Developer combined net worth over 25% of TDC

Guarantor net liquid assets over 10% of TDC

criteria.note: Four independent tests, one tier each: 2 + 2.5 + 6 + 7.5 = 18. Minimums: 12 for MBP/RHW, 14 with FHA Risk Sharing (p.57), 10 for the Infill and Redevelopment Pool (p.58).

criteria.heading: Nonprofits, Public Housing Authorities, and Local Small Businesses
criteria.quote: Projects shall be eligible for a maximum of fourteen (14) points under this section as detailed

tiers.tier_label: Category 1: NP or PHA with controlling (51%+) ownership, Qualified Nonprofit
Category 2: PHA, Local Small Business or Community-Based NP with 10.1-15% GP/MM interest
Category 3: per NP/PHA/Local Small Business as general contractor, architect or property manager (max 8)
Category 4: per entity on Secondary Development Team (max 8)
Category 4: per entity in another capacity-building role (max 8)

criteria.note: Four categories capped at 8, 6, 8 and 8 (30 in all) under a section maximum of 14; the same entity may score in several. No points if the entity is on the Primary Development Team and earns under 50% of its 4.1.1 points; 4.1.2 deductions carry over (p.66). The Scoring Summary Table (p.59) names this item 'Nonprofits (NPs), Public Housing Authorities (PHAs) and Minority/ Disadvantaged Business Enterprises (MBE/DBEs)'; the body names Local Small Businesses and does not mention MBE/DBEs. Recorded, not resolved.

Feedback, conflict resolution and privacy protocols

criteria.note: (market rate units / affordable units) x 10, rounded to 1/100. No cap is written into the formula; 10 is the stated maximum.

criteria.quote: 1. One (1) point will be awarded to projects that involve “twinning” of 9% LIHTC and

tiers.tier_label: Twinning: three highest-scoring twinning projects, 150+ units, $5M+ MBP need
Top three projects in communities of opportunity in the Baltimore Region and DC Metro
Top two projects in the listed non-metro counties
Joint development with MDOT or WMATA on transit-adjacent land

criteria.note: Six items worth 11 under a section maximum of 4. Several are awarded only to the top projects in the round, ranked on final scores excluding 4.4.6 and 4.8 (p.80).

criteria.heading: Direct Leveraging
criteria.quote: DHCD will award points based on the percentage of total development costs funded by non-state
criteria.note: Share of TDC from non-State sources divided by .06667 (non-rural) or .06 (rural, then capped at 15). Twinning projects of 120+ units with a $5M+ MBP need 'will receive two (2) additional points' (p.82); whether those can take the score above 15 is not said. Coded at the stated maximum of 15.

criteria.heading: Operating Subsidies
criteria.quote: DHCD recognizes that projects may include other federal or local investments not directly
criteria.note: (Average subsidy per affordable unit per year / $600) x 10 in entitlement jurisdictions, / $300 in non-entitlement. The worked example (p.85) computes '$375 ÷ $600 = 0.625' and then '0.9375 x 10 = 6.25 points awarded': 0.625 x 10 would be 6.25; 0.9375 is not derived anywhere. Recorded, not resolved.

criteria.note: (excess over cost limit / cost limit) x 8 for large projects, x 6 for small (up to 40 units). Cost limits are published separately before each round.

criteria.heading: State Bonus Points
criteria.quote: No more than ten (10) State Bonus Points may be awarded to any project, except for

tiers.tier_label: Intergenerational, elderly, or permanent supportive housing

criteria.note: Discretionary and optional; only projects scoring at least 120 before bonus are eligible, and no more than 20% of competitive LIHTC and RHFP funds may go to bonus recipients. Outside the 221-point scale per the Scoring Summary Table, which gives '(maximum of 10 points)'; the body allows 15 for intergenerational, elderly or supportive housing. Recorded, not resolved; coded at 15 on its own track.
